<!-- pr-reviewer: 2fd7df09516c668f3321b4a523e0d2c66c792fd4 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The change affects posted G-code.

The script and MCP paths now use the existing per-operation post functions. These functions check the whole program before they write files. The combined-program paths refuse `per_op` by name. The result types describe the new output. The decision file records the choice.

Local results against upstream main `e3ca44fa705d71438a8fd8a8efccbafcc2b6517f`:

- The trial merge was clean. This head already contains that main.
- The selected app targets built with `cargo test --no-run`.
- App library: 350 passed, 1 ignored.
- `between_setups`: 10 passed.
- `scripting`: 19 passed.
- `per_op_files`: 9 passed.
- `setup_post_options`: 11 passed.
- `setup_mounts_post`: 8 passed.
- `mcp`: 22 passed.
- `mcp_post_options`: 5 passed.
- `posting`: 17 passed.
- `unwritten_post`: 3 passed.
- `cli`: 12 passed.
- Total: 466 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

I repeated two mutations in the local review worktree:

1. I restored `script/api.rs` from upstream main. The new MCP and scripting tests each failed because the combined post refused `per_op`.
2. I removed the `single` guard in `posting_mounts.rs`. The new combined-API test failed because `post_setup` returned success.

I restored both files. The full `between_setups` and `scripting` suites then passed again: 29 passed. The worktree has no code changes.

No NC, CL, or golden files changed. No UI files changed, so screenshots are not required. I checked the current upstream main rules.

Requested changes: none.

Scope: I ran the quick-gate plan and the selected suites above. I did not run all 187 suites in that plan, the full gate, or the desktop GUI. I used no GitHub runner.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
